topSignals.title: Germany's EnEfG data-center rules take final shape ahead of autumn Bundestag debate.
topSignals.text: The Bundeskabinett's June 24 draft amendment (parliamentary passage expected this autumn) sets PUE ceilings of 1.6/1.4 (mid-2027/2030) for existing data centers and 1.2 for new builds with a doubled four-year grace period, raises the in-scope threshold to 500 kW installed IT power, and pushes the 100%-renewable-electricity mandate from 2027 to 2030. Directly relevant to opex/design assumptions for any SOFC-CHP data-center case in Germany or the EU - see LCOE section below. DENEFF | FPS Law | Gleiss Lutz

topSignals.title: Ceres Power spins out its flow-battery unit as "Certain Energy" after a GBP10m raise (August 26).
topSignals.text: RFC Power, Ceres' manganese flow-battery subsidiary for long-duration storage, closed a GBP10m (approx. $13.6m) Series A led by the British Business Bank with Centrica and Temasek Trust's Catalytic Capital participating; Ceres retains approximately 37% equity, a revenue share, and a board seat. A capital-light way for a cash-constrained SOFC/SOEC licensor to keep a toehold in adjacent storage tech, not a core-technology announcement. Investegate | Proactive Investors

topSignals.title: Bloom Energy: stock extends its Pelosi-linked rally; Q3 2026 earnings date now confirmed for October 27.
topSignals.text: BE rose another 3.2% today, continuing the run triggered by the August 21 disclosure of Nancy Pelosi's household position; consensus for the October 27 report sits at $0.64 EPS (vs. $0.15 a year ago) and approx. $1.07B revenue (vs. $519M). A modest, calendar-driven update - no new operating catalyst behind today's move. Investing.com

items.text: Elcogen (priority): Confirmed quiet via direct newsroom check (elcogen.com/category/news) - no post since June 30. Other items surfaced today (SYRIUS Horizon Europe steel-decarbonization project, a new CTO appointment, TIME Top GreenTech recognition) all predate that and are already on file. Status unchanged: E3000 G2 in volume production at ELCO I Tallinn (360 MW/yr). Elcogen News

Topsoe (priority): Confirmed quiet via direct site check (topsoe.com/news) - no stack- or SOEC-specific post found beyond the ammonia/SAF items already noted August 25-26. Herning SOEC factory hibernation and the 2029+ SOFC data-center pathway are unchanged. Topsoe News
Ceres Power (update): Spins out flow-battery unit RFC Power as Certain Energy - see Top Signal #2. A diversification move in adjacent long-duration storage, not a core SOFC/SOEC announcement.

Other players: No new stack/cell-level announcements from Bloom, FuelCell Energy, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, Aisin, or Convion in the last 24-48h beyond items covered under Market & Financials.
Germany EnEfG: see Top Signal #1 for full detail.

Project Jupiter (NM): Following the August 23 stay, NMED confirmed it is preparing its required Supreme Court response (due September 2) and released a draft version of its administrative record, stating this gives the public "ample time to review, regardless of how the timeline moves forward." No ruling yet; the September 14 hearing remains contingent on the stay's outcome. KRQE | Source NM

PJM/FERC large-load rules: No new order. PJM's Interim Resource Adequacy Service proposal for large loads without their own power supply and the Reliability Backstop Procurement (see August 26 digest) remain pending at FERC; the RM26-4 comment window is still tracking toward mid-September.

US tax credits: No change to 45V ($0.60/kg maximum credit, production must begin before 2028) or 48E (30% ITC, domestic-content thresholds stepping 45%/2026 -> 50%/2027 -> 55%/2028) - both unchanged from prior digests.

Ceres Power (CWR.L): RFC Power/Certain Energy spinout - see Top Signal #2. Goldman Sachs' Conviction Buy (168% upside, flagged August 25) unchanged. H1 2026 interim results still have no announced date (last year's equivalent: September 26, 2025).
Bloom Energy (BE): +3.2% today - see Top Signal #3. Next earnings confirmed for October 27, 2026.
FuelCell Energy (FCEL): Q3 2026 results call confirmed for September 2, 10:00 a.m. ET (unchanged from August 25).

lcoe.text: Germany EnEfG thresholds (✓ sourced, not my calculation): PUE <=1.6 (mid-2027) / <=1.4 (2030) for existing data centers (vs. 1.5/1.3 previously planned), <=1.2 for new builds with the compliance grace period doubled to four years; 100%-renewable-electricity mandate deferred from 2027 to 2030; in-scope threshold raised to 500 kW installed IT power (from 300 kW connection capacity). Relevant to opex/design assumptions for any EU SOFC-CHP data-center case. See Top Signal #1.

Ceres RFC Power/Certain Energy raise (✎ my conversion, not primary-sourced): GBP10m ≈ $13.6m at today's spot rate (GBP/USD 1.3642, xe.com). A data point on capital-raising appetite/cost for SOFC-adjacent players diversifying into storage, not a direct LCOE input.
Gas price case: EIA's August STEO figures ($3.44/MMBtu 2026 average, $3.03/MMBtu remaining five months, approx. $2.87/MMBtu Q3 2026 Henry Hub) unchanged from prior digests.

Pending carry-forward: PJM Expedited Interconnection Track, PJM large-load rules (IRAS/BYONG) at FERC, FERC RM26-4 (mid-September comment window), Bloom 10-Q MW-shipped/ASP extraction (September 11), Bloom scandium class-action deadline (September 28), Ceres H1 2026 results (September, unconfirmed date), Bloom Q3 2026 earnings (now confirmed October 27), FCEL Q3 2026 results call (September 2), Rolls-Royce SMR GDA DAC (Q4 2026/Q1 2027 estimate), Germany EnEfG Bundestag/Bundesrat vote (autumn 2026), NM Project Jupiter Supreme Court response deadline (September 2).
